method: Dynamic theme priority is based on two separate questions: WHAT'S NEW (fresh material evidence/catalyst/price confirmation) and WHAT MATTERS MOST NOW (current cross-asset, sector, earnings, inflation/rates and portfolio transmission). Historical importance alone does not keep a theme near the top.

whatsNewNow: Global long-end yields are breaking higher at the same time as energy/product inflation remains elevated, turning duration and financing quality into the immediate market gate.
Americas crude and US LNG are gaining strategic relevance as buyers diversify away from Gulf concentration; this is broader than a one-day oil spike.
Agriculture/fertilizer is moving from background scarcity toward a live investment theme as El Nino/weather risk, fertilizer affordability and crop-input elasticity collide.
Software is showing selective relative strength versus hardware, but only companies with real AI monetisation, security/workflow control and cash-flow growth deserve promotion.
whatMattersMostNow: Bond yields / term premium and energy inflation
AI physical infrastructure with a much higher cost-of-capital hurdle
Selective software rotation beneath range-bound headline indices

september-bond-oil-crowding.whyNow: The market is simultaneously confronting higher US/Japan long yields, energy inflation and crowded positioning. That combination changes the hurdle rate for almost every Power Stack equity and is already visible in rate-sensitive breadth.
september-bond-oil-crowding.marketTransmission: Higher discount rates punish leverage and long-duration optionality while oil/product inflation supports current-cash-flow scarcity businesses. Small caps, homebuilders and weaker balance sheets are the key stress tell.
september-bond-oil-crowding.confirmation: US10Y sustains above ~4.8%, oil/product strength persists and breadth weakens beneath the indices.
september-bond-oil-crowding.invalidation: Long yields reverse materially, energy inflation fades and breadth broadens without credit deterioration.
september-bond-oil-crowding.nextTest: US labour/ISM data, Treasury curve reaction, oil/product prices and post-Labor-Day equity breadth.
september-bond-oil-crowding.watchlistAction: Raise the entry-price hurdle for expensive duration; favour CF/CTVA/BG/CCJ/LNG and cash-generative physical bottlenecks over speculative AI beta.

long-end-duration-stress.whyNow: US 10-year yields are near the upper end of the recent range while Japan's long end is also repricing. The long end, not simply the next Fed meeting, is setting equity duration and financing costs.
long-end-duration-stress.marketTransmission: Valuation compression for AI/cloud/SMR/high-capex stories; higher refinancing costs; pressure on housing and weaker credit; preference for near-term FCF and contracted backlog.
long-end-duration-stress.confirmation: US10Y/30Y and global long yields continue making higher highs while real yields/term premium remain elevated.
long-end-duration-stress.invalidation: A durable bond rally lowers real yields and credit stress without a growth collapse.
long-end-duration-stress.nextTest: Treasury auctions, inflation expectations versus nominal yields, ISM/jobs and credit-spread behaviour.
long-end-duration-stress.watchlistAction: Keep PWR/ETN/GEV high-quality but valuation-disciplined; penalise NBIS/SPCX/SMR-style financing dependence.

refining-product-inflation.whyNow: Renewed Iran escalation keeps the physical energy shock live, while diesel/jet and refinery economics remain more important to inflation transmission than crude alone.
refining-product-inflation.marketTransmission: Transport/freight and industrial input costs rise; refiners/logistics can outperform; airlines/cruises/consumer cyclicals face margin pressure; the inflation impulse feeds directly back into yields.
refining-product-inflation.confirmation: Middle-distillate cracks, distillate inventories and freight remain tight even if crude pauses.
refining-product-inflation.invalidation: Hormuz normalises and product cracks/inventories revert quickly enough to remove the inflation channel.
refining-product-inflation.nextTest: Hormuz vessel flows, ULSD/jet cracks, EIA inventories, refinery outages and demand destruction.
refining-product-inflation.watchlistAction: XOM/HIBISCS remain useful owned exposures; do not chase pure oil beta. Keep VLO/MPC/STNG as tactical rather than permanent compounder trades.

energy-security-americas-lng.whyNow: The war is accelerating buyer diversification toward Western Hemisphere crude and US LNG. The rerouting can outlast the immediate conflict because security of supply has acquired a higher strategic value.
energy-security-americas-lng.marketTransmission: Higher utilisation and strategic value for US LNG/export infrastructure, Americas crude, pipelines and long-haul logistics; potential capex rerouting toward reliable supply basins.
energy-security-americas-lng.confirmation: Americas export volumes, US LNG utilisation/contracts and European/Asian diversification stay elevated after spot-war volatility cools.
energy-security-americas-lng.invalidation: Rapid Gulf normalisation plus new LNG oversupply collapses spreads and long-term contracting momentum.
energy-security-americas-lng.nextTest: European gas/storage, Qatar/Gulf exports, Cheniere utilisation/contracts and Americas-to-Asia flows.
energy-security-americas-lng.watchlistAction: LNG moves into the top opportunity tier, but near resistance it remains pullback-first rather than chase-now.

ai-physical-bottlenecks.whyNow: Orders and backlog still validate power, transmission, switchgear and cooling as real bottlenecks, but rising yields mean the market is demanding cash conversion rather than paying any price for the theme.
ai-physical-bottlenecks.marketTransmission: Supplier backlogs and pricing remain strong, while financing-sensitive developers and high-multiple beneficiaries become more vulnerable to duration compression.
ai-physical-bottlenecks.confirmation: PWR/ETN/GEV/TT/MOD/ECL order growth and backlog convert to revenue, margins and FCF despite higher rates.
ai-physical-bottlenecks.invalidation: Hyperscaler cancellations, grid interconnection deferrals or supplier book-to-bill/backlog deterioration.
ai-physical-bottlenecks.nextTest: Supplier orders, backlog conversion, hyperscaler capex and data-centre interconnection/cooling commitments.
ai-physical-bottlenecks.watchlistAction: Keep PWR/ETN high-quality; demand better entries because portfolio exposure already includes YTLPOWR.

fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.whyNow: Nitrogen scarcity, weather risk and crop-input affordability are converging. Food demand is resilient, but farmers can still optimise input use, making producer feedstock advantage and input elasticity decisive.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.marketTransmission: North American nitrogen margins can benefit from global scarcity; high fertilizer costs can later tighten crop supply; phosphate producers remain exposed to sulphur/input-cost pressure.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.confirmation: Global nitrogen remains firm while North American gas advantage persists and farmer application cuts do not overwhelm realised pricing.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.invalidation: Fertilizer prices collapse, Gulf production normalises rapidly or crop economics trigger much larger demand destruction than expected.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.nextTest: Urea/ammonia prices, Henry Hub, India/Brazil demand, application rates and crop-to-input price ratios.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.watchlistAction: CF becomes the preferred commodity-agriculture expression; CTVA/BG add higher-quality portfolio diversification.

ai-financing-cash-conversion.whyNow: The bond selloff makes financing structure a first-order variable for the AI buildout. Strong demand no longer excuses poor per-share cash economics.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.marketTransmission: Debt/convertible-heavy builders suffer a higher hurdle rate and dilution risk; cash-rich incumbents and suppliers with customer funding/backlog gain relative quality.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.confirmation: More debt/convertible/lease financing, weak FCF conversion or delayed utilisation at AI infrastructure developers.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.invalidation: Cash conversion improves rapidly and financing costs fall without cancellations.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.nextTest: NBIS/CoreWeave-style funding, capex-to-revenue, utilisation, lease commitments and customer prepayments.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.watchlistAction: Demote financing-dependent AI infrastructure relative to ETN/PWR/GEV/TT and current-cash-flow scarcity ideas.

software-relative-strength.whyNow: Salesforce and CrowdStrike delivered strong operating evidence while software began separating from semiconductors. The rotation is selective rather than a blanket SaaS rerating.
software-relative-strength.marketTransmission: Capital can rotate from crowded hardware into software platforms with AI monetisation, security/workflow control and strong FCF. High real yields still punish weak or purely narrative SaaS.
software-relative-strength.confirmation: Software breadth and relative strength persist while CRM/CRWD/NOW fundamentals continue to beat and cash flow expands.
software-relative-strength.invalidation: Post-earnings gains fail broadly or higher yields compress the sector without earnings revisions offsetting the multiple.
software-relative-strength.nextTest: CRM follow-through, CRWD/NOW FCF and ARR, software-vs-SOXX relative strength and real yields.
software-relative-strength.watchlistAction: Add CRM/CRWD as pullback watches, not chase entries after large earnings gaps.

power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.whyNow: The data-centre bottleneck has broadened from generation to reliability, backup power and power quality. Large contracted orders validate the spend, but it is now partly nested inside the broader AI physical-infrastructure theme.
power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.marketTransmission: Demand for backup generation, UPS, switchgear, battery systems and power-quality equipment rises as grid reliability/interconnection become constraints.
power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.confirmation: GNRC/POWL/ETN/VRT orders and hyperscaler backlog remain strong.
power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.invalidation: Data-centre capacity additions slow materially or backup/power-quality orders normalize sharply.
power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.nextTest: Hyperscaler backup-power awards, lead times and backlog conversion.
power-reliability-around-the-bottleneck.watchlistAction: Keep GNRC/POWL in the research universe; do not force them above better-diversifying opportunities.

copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.whyNow: Copper demand remains tied to grid/data-centre capex, but recent price action still contains tariff/inventory and positioning distortions. The structural thesis is stronger than the immediate entry setup.
copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.marketTransmission: Higher copper supports miners but raises input costs for cables/electrical equipment; tariff/inventory flows can temporarily overwhelm fundamentals.
copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.confirmation: Physical stocks remain tight and demand/TC-RC/mine evidence validates price strength beyond positioning.
copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.invalidation: Inventories rebuild materially and global/China demand weakens enough to break the structural deficit thesis.
copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.nextTest: LME/COMEX stocks and spreads, China demand, mine disruptions and US tariff policy.
copper-scarcity-squeeze-risk.watchlistAction: FCX stays wait-for-pullback; no FOMO near resistance.

spr-replenishment-energy-security.whyNow: A depleted US emergency buffer makes every renewed Gulf escalation more inflation-sensitive and increases the eventual strategic value of domestic supply/storage/logistics.
spr-replenishment-energy-security.marketTransmission: Less policy cushion in an emergency; longer-run support for domestic barrels, storage, pipelines and Gulf Coast logistics if replenishment follows the crisis.
spr-replenishment-energy-security.confirmation: SPR remains historically low and DOE begins meaningful refill/energy-security actions.
spr-replenishment-energy-security.invalidation: Large emergency releases or rapid geopolitical normalisation remove the buffer constraint.
spr-replenishment-energy-security.nextTest: Weekly SPR stocks, DOE policy/tenders and domestic logistics utilisation.
spr-replenishment-energy-security.watchlistAction: Supports XOM/CVX/KMI/WMB but is not enough alone to justify chasing oil equities.

water-food-energy-collision.whyNow: El Nino and regional rainfall deficits keep water as a second-order constraint across crops, power and industry, but immediate market transmission is weaker than bonds/oil/fertilizer.
water-food-energy-collision.marketTransmission: Crop yields, hydro/nuclear output and industrial water constraints can lift demand for reuse, treatment, irrigation and municipal infrastructure.
water-food-energy-collision.confirmation: Drought/rainfall deficits persist and start changing crop/power output or municipal capex.
water-food-energy-collision.invalidation: Weather normalises before supply/earnings transmission becomes material.
water-food-energy-collision.nextTest: India/Asia rainfall, crop forecasts, river levels and water-infrastructure orders.
water-food-energy-collision.watchlistAction: VMI/XYL/ECL remain quality crossovers; VMI gets the most direct agri + grid optionality.

ammonia-logistics-storage.whyNow: Fertilizer and Gulf rerouting keep specialised ammonia/gas shipping relevant, but it is a narrower second-order expression than CF/BG/LNG.
ammonia-logistics-storage.marketTransmission: Longer routes raise vessel utilisation and specialised terminal/storage value.
ammonia-logistics-storage.confirmation: TCE rates/utilisation and replacement routes remain elevated.
ammonia-logistics-storage.invalidation: Hormuz normalises and freight economics rapidly revert.
ammonia-logistics-storage.nextTest: NVGS TCE/utilisation, ammonia freight and terminal occupancy.
ammonia-logistics-storage.watchlistAction: Keep NVGS/Vopak as specialist research, below the narrow primary watchlist.

industrial-automation-first.whyNow: Warehouse/fixed automation continues to produce real revenue and profit, but the theme is not currently driving the broad market the way rates, energy and agriculture are.
industrial-automation-first.marketTransmission: Industrial capex and labour-productivity spending support automation; humanoid valuations remain more sensitive to rates and hype.
industrial-automation-first.confirmation: SYM/ROK/CGNX/Geekplus orders, deployments and margins keep improving.
industrial-automation-first.invalidation: Industrial capex rolls over or deployments fail to translate to margins/cash flow.
industrial-automation-first.nextTest: SYM deployment growth, warehouse orders and factory capex.
industrial-automation-first.watchlistAction: SYM remains the most interesting pure commercial automation candidate, but not a top macro-driven allocation today.

ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.whyNow: HBM/packaging remains a genuine AI bottleneck, but current market leadership is rotating away from a pure hardware scarcity narrative.
ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.marketTransmission: Packaging capacity and HBM pricing affect system delivery/cost, but semiconductor-cycle concentration raises portfolio overlap.
ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.confirmation: HBM pricing and TCB/hybrid-bonding orders stay tight with customer-funded capacity.
ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.invalidation: Packaging/HBM capacity normalises faster than AI demand.
ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.nextTest: AMKR/ASMPT orders, HBM pricing and customer prepayments.
ai-memory-packaging-bottleneck.watchlistAction: Keep AMKR/ASMPT research-active, but below diversified physical bottlenecks and new scarcity themes.

china-fiscal-infrastructure.whyNow: Selective fiscal infrastructure remains more credible than broad China reflation, but no new policy impulse currently warrants a top ranking.
china-fiscal-infrastructure.marketTransmission: Supports grid/power/nuclear and selected industrial capex without guaranteeing a broad consumer/property beta rally.
china-fiscal-infrastructure.confirmation: Faster special-bond execution translates into orders/power demand.
china-fiscal-infrastructure.invalidation: Fiscal execution stalls or policy rotates away from strategic infrastructure.
china-fiscal-infrastructure.nextTest: China fiscal outlays, power demand, special bonds and new nuclear/grid approvals.
china-fiscal-infrastructure.watchlistAction: Keep 0836/1816/1072 selective; do not promote broad China beta.

ai-industrial-networking.whyNow: Industrial/data-centre networking remains a real picks-and-shovels layer but is currently nested within the broader physical AI buildout rather than independently driving markets.
ai-industrial-networking.marketTransmission: Connectivity and industrial Ethernet demand rise with data-centre/factory automation buildout.
ai-industrial-networking.invalidation: Industrial/data-centre capex slows or network content fails to scale.
ai-industrial-networking.watchlistAction: BDC remains a quality universe name, not a top narrow-watchlist allocation.

aluminium-western-scarcity.whyNow: Western physical availability remains tight, but Chinese semi/alloy exports have muted benchmark transmission and no fresh shock currently puts aluminium above copper/fertilizer.
aluminium-western-scarcity.marketTransmission: Regional premiums and producer earnings can benefit even when LME headline pricing looks calmer.
aluminium-western-scarcity.confirmation: Western inventories/premiums tighten further despite Chinese exports.
aluminium-western-scarcity.invalidation: Gulf supply recovers and LME stocks rebuild.
aluminium-western-scarcity.nextTest: LME stocks, regional premiums and China semi/alloy exports.

north-american-electrical-localisation.whyNow: Localisation remains strategically useful but is currently a supporting mechanism beneath the larger grid/electrical bottleneck theme.
north-american-electrical-localisation.marketTransmission: Qualified domestic electrical capacity gains pricing/security value under tariff volatility.
north-american-electrical-localisation.confirmation: Tariffs/sourcing rules materially shift orders to domestic suppliers.
north-american-electrical-localisation.invalidation: Trade frictions ease with no sourcing change.
north-american-electrical-localisation.nextTest: Tariff scope, sourcing commentary and domestic utilisation.
north-american-electrical-localisation.watchlistAction: Supportive for ETN/POWL/HUBB/BDC, not an independent allocation trigger.

personalized-oncology.whyNow: The Phase 3 signal remains scientifically material, but absent new detailed data it is no longer among the market's dominant developing stories.
personalized-oncology.marketTransmission: Mainly company/biotech-specific rather than broad cross-asset transmission.
personalized-oncology.confirmation: Detailed efficacy/OS/regulatory data broaden the platform thesis.
personalized-oncology.invalidation: Detailed data or regulatory feedback disappoints.
personalized-oncology.nextTest: Full Phase 3 data and regulatory path.
personalized-oncology.watchlistAction: Keep MRK/MRNA in background research; no current Power Stack capital-priority promotion.

beef-cycle-spread-reversal.whyNow: Policy-driven lean-beef relief is still worth monitoring, but the story has not become a broad market driver and MCD traffic matters more than beef alone.
beef-cycle-spread-reversal.marketTransmission: Restaurant/input margins and packer spreads, not broad macro pricing.
beef-cycle-spread-reversal.confirmation: Cattle/trim costs fall faster than menu/boxed-beef pricing and company margins improve.
beef-cycle-spread-reversal.invalidation: Herd scarcity keeps costs high or consumer traffic weakens enough to offset input relief.
beef-cycle-spread-reversal.nextTest: Cattle/trim spreads, MCD traffic and processor margins.
beef-cycle-spread-reversal.watchlistAction: MCD remains a quality background watch, not a top current theme allocation.

sanctions-maritime-intelligence.whyNow: Sanctions complexity is rising again with Iran escalation, but the target-market equity expression remains poor.
sanctions-maritime-intelligence.marketTransmission: Higher compliance and trade-monitoring costs across banks, insurers and shipping.
sanctions-maritime-intelligence.confirmation: Sanctions expand into more vessels/banks/intermediaries and listed data vendors show revenue traction.
sanctions-maritime-intelligence.nextTest: OFAC packages and evidence of monetisation by listed vendors.

marine-war-risk-insurance.directionOfTravel: stable but no clean target equity
marine-war-risk-insurance.whyNow: War-risk cover remains part of the Hormuz transmission chain but is already captured more cleanly through energy/logistics themes.
marine-war-risk-insurance.marketTransmission: Premiums/coverage affect vessel availability and route economics.
marine-war-risk-insurance.confirmation: Insurance exclusions or state-backed cover become binding constraints on trade.
marine-war-risk-insurance.nextTest: War-risk premiums, exclusions and government support.

rubber-acreage-squeeze.whyNow: The long-run acreage story remains plausible, but it has little present cross-market transmission and no current Power Stack capital priority.
rubber-acreage-squeeze.marketTransmission: Mostly tire/input economics and selected Asian producer margins.
rubber-acreage-squeeze.confirmation: Rubber prices/utilisation and producer earnings accelerate materially.
rubber-acreage-squeeze.invalidation: Supply response or weak tire demand absorbs the acreage decline.
rubber-acreage-squeeze.nextTest: STA volumes/utilisation, TSR20/SIR20 and China tire demand.
